reasons: Both answers open with the right correction (the cap is 6 points, so 10 can only drop to 4) and give the correct 3 hours of online study plus 6 exams (20 questions, 18 to pass, 2 retakes). Both explain that 4 points remaining is not safe, and that the points clear on the clearing date if the period ends under 12 points with fines paid. I opened the gov.cn gazette text of the measures (the page B cites) and confirmed Articles 15, 17, 18, 25, 26 and 27 and the fraud fines A cites. I also opened the Shenzhen police page B cites, which says study time cannot be accumulated to earn exam attempts, so B's claim is verified. A covers more of the key: the on-site (1 hour for 2 points) and public-activity (1 hour for 1 point) routes with the shared 6-point cap, and the full list of ineligibility conditions. B skips key point 5 and is thinner on key point 6, though B's application step (face recognition, then review) matches key point 7 more closely. Both are long and carry some Beijing-specific detail, and B adds invented minute estimates for application time. A is slightly more complete against the key, so A wins by a slight margin.
